info.name: B4F Board API
info.description:
B4F Board API — all 21 current controller operations. MongoDB-backed Projects, Workspaces and Issues, plus JWT authentication. Updated from Nest Swagger metadata and controller/DTO/service source.

Set baseUrl, internalToolKey, authEmail and authPassword privately before use. Login captures accessToken; /auth/me uses Bearer authentication. The JWT currently expires after 2 hours. All nine resource write endpoints use Bearer JWT authentication. Only GET /projects/stats keeps x-internal-tool-key; a JWT alone does not grant stats access.

Optional list filters are present but disabled. Enable them in Params. Run folders in order: Auth, Projects, Workspaces, Issues, Deletes. Creates generate unique keys/slugs and capture numeric ids; Deletes removes only the captured targets, issues first. Register leaves an account in the database (no user-delete endpoint exists); for an existing account, skip Register and use Login. Run only against an intended test database when running the whole collection. Environment variables override collection values; remove id/key/slug overrides when using automatic chaining.

Saved examples are illustrative, not captures from the current database. Existing examples and status assertions have been retained and refreshed for MongoDB and access-control behavior. See README.md beside this file for setup and verification limitations.

item.name: Deletes
item.description: Permanently deletes captured test targets, issue first. Empty default delete ids prevent accidentally targeting a seed record. No cascading delete exists.

request.description:
Delete an issue.

Source: Swagger operation IssuesController_remove.

Path id is a numeric application id (not MongoDB _id). Malformed id: 400. Missing record: 404.

Requires Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}} from Login. Missing, invalid, or expired token: 401. The old internal-tool key alone does not authenticate these routes.

Permanently deletes and returns the document (200). No cascading deletion. Create the corresponding test record first; its response captures this delete target.
